detail: Dashboard: created native Bevy 0.15 + bevy_egui 0.33 visualization app in dashboard/. 4 source files: main.rs (camera, orbit controls, lighting), data.rs (CLI polling, event log reading, LegendData resource), graph.rs (3D force-directed layout, node spheres, gizmo edges, salience-based emissive glow, pulsing animation), panels.rs (egui side panels: event log, memory stats, short-term entries with salience bars, session log). Zero errors, zero warnings. Compiles clean.

Dashboard WSL→Windows launch: added legend dashboard CLI command that auto-detects WSL, converts Linux paths to \\wsl.localhost UNC paths, and launches the cross-compiled Windows .exe. Dashboard receives --project-dir and uses wsl.exe to run legend commands inside WSL for data polling. Cross-compiled to x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (110MB release exe). Updated copilot-instructions.md with dashboard section.

Dashboard working! Cross-compiled Bevy exe launches from WSL via cmd.exe /C start with Stdio::null() — fully detaches from WSL fds, no more read failed 5 errors. User confirmed window is visible on Windows desktop with 3D graph rendering.

Architecture: Legend has three memory layers — immediate buffer (FIFO, 256 cap), short-term vector store (cosine similarity, salience decay, 1024 cap), and long-term knowledge graph (Hebbian reinforcement, 2048 nodes, 8192 edges). Data flows upward: tick writes to immediate+short-term, consolidate merges into graph.

Key source files: src/memory/mod.rs is the core engine (MemoryState, tick, retrieve_context, consolidate, prune). src/memory/embed.rs handles n-gram embeddings and cosine similarity. src/memory/extract.rs does code-aware entity extraction. src/memory/summarize.rs does extractive summarization with decision-rationale boosting.

Decision: chose Bevy over egui-only because we wanted true 3D force-directed graph with orbit camera, not just flat 2D panels. Bevy gives us PBR materials with emissive glow for salience, gizmo lines for edges, and proper 3D transforms for node positioning.

User preference: wants native app, not web UI. WSL environment means cross-compiling to Windows exe via x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target with mingw linker. Launch via cmd.exe /C start to avoid fd inheritance issues.

Implemented node click inspection in dashboard: SelectedNode resource, raycasting click detection with egui passthrough, highlight_selected system (white glow on selected, blue glow on neighbors, cyan edges), inspection panel showing node details + clickable neighbor navigation

Enriched node inspector to 3-column layout: (1) Properties — ID, weight, salience bar, last_seen, age in ticks, degree (in/out), avg edge weight, strongest neighbor, mention counts. (2) Related Memories — short-term entries whose text contains the node label, with salience bars + usage + access time; plus session log mentions. (3) Connections — neighbors sorted by edge weight descending, with kind badges, edge weight, edge kind, neighbor node weight.

Implemented 4 major features for fresh-project readiness: (1) Reconsolidation — retrieved memories become labile for 5 ticks; if next tick is related, updates the existing memory in-place instead of duplicating. Tracks reconsolidation_count. (2) Memory importance detection — MemoryCategory enum (Decision/Architecture/Bug/Todo/Preference/Progress/General) with classify_text(). Enhanced compute_salience with 2x decision/bug scoring. (3) Associative priming — retrieve_context extracts entities from retrieved short-term entries, follows graph edges 1-hop to surface related nodes the query alone wouldn't match. (4) Categorized start summary — build_start_summary groups memories by category for scannable cold-start. Dashboard shows labile (yellow ⚡) and reconsolidation count (🔄×N) badges. 79 tests, 0 warnings.

New project: improving Stickler's design sense. Stickler is a TypeScript/Playwright autonomous UI testing tool. Currently it can validate user flows (text-matching against success/fail signals) but is completely blind to visual quality. Screenshots are captured but NEVER analyzed — no CSS extraction, no layout analysis, no visual assertions. The plan is to iterate on Stickler until it can evaluate design quality, not just functional correctness. Legend is being used as the memory system for this work.

TUI Dashboard Design Decision: Option C (Focus + sidebar layout). Stats sidebar on left shows Clock/ST/Nodes/Edges/Labile count + keybind hints. Main panel takes rest of space for active view (Short-term Memory, Graph Browser, Events, etc). Features: live refresh (1-3s polling), vim keybindings (j/k/gg/G), search with /, node drill-down with Enter, query tester with :q <text>. Default to TUI, allow --3d flag for full Bevy dashboard. Using Ratatui for implementation.

Implemented TUI dashboard using Ratatui. Features: sidebar with stats (Clock, ST entries, Nodes, Edges, Labile count) + keybind hints. Main panel with 3 views (Short-Term Memory, Knowledge Graph, Session Events). Vim keybindings (j/k nav, g/G jump, Tab view switch, 1-3 direct view). Query mode (:) runs memory queries inline. Search mode (/) for filtering. Auto-refresh every 2s. CLI: 'legend dashboard' launches TUI, 'legend dashboard --3d' launches Bevy.
fn process_data() uses struct Config for settings

Migration complete: Implemented migrate_corrupt_backup() in src/memory/mod.rs. When new fields (current_task, ticks_since_consolidation) were added to MemoryState, old bincode-serialized memory failed to load. The migration function defines a MemoryStateV1 struct matching the old format, deserializes the .corrupt backup, converts to new format, saves, and removes the backup. Successfully recovered 3 short-term entries, 174 graph nodes, 5171 edges from the backup.
Implemented TUI graph drill-down: Enter drills into neighbors list with stack-based back (b/backspace), detail view via 'd', graph list shows edge types and dynamic title.

Token-efficiency pass: memory outputs now compact JSON; start summary trimmed to context+categorized only, with lower caps (sessions 5, top nodes 8, per-category 5) and shorter text (120). Updated tests/help text accordingly.
Smoke test: compact JSON outputs for start/query/context, and trimmed summary sizes look correct.

Bug discovered: Legend looks for .legend/ directory in current working directory, causing errors when run outside of an initialized project. Need to add init check or better error handling.

Reviewed init.rs setup - currently supports Claude Code (.claude), Codex (.codex), and Copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md) hooks. Need to verify these work and potentially add Gemini/Zed support.
Decision: Add Zed and Gemini support to init.rs. Implement smart command detection - use 'cargo run --quiet --' when in Legend source dir, 'legend' CLI otherwise.
Research complete: Zed supports .rules, .github/copilot-instructions.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md. Gemini Code Assist uses .gemini/styleguide.md. Will add setup for both.

Implemented Zed (.rules) and Gemini (.gemini/styleguide.md) support in init.rs. Added smart command detection: uses 'legend' CLI in normal projects, 'cargo run --quiet --' in Legend source dir (detected via Cargo.toml). Tested successfully in both contexts.

Updated instruction template to use 'memory start' for session init (better than query). Added dashboard launch instructions, memory sessions command, and reinforce command. Rebuilt and installed updated binary.

Session summary: Successfully added Zed and Gemini support to Legend init. Smart command detection works (uses 'legend' in normal projects, 'cargo run --quiet --' in Legend source). Updated instruction templates to match best practices (memory start, dashboard, etc.). Supports: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Zed, and Gemini Code Assist.
Built release version and installed updated Legend binary globally to ~/.cargo/bin. Ready for user testing.
